LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 ESSAY WRITING – DESCRIPTIVE COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Essay writing – Descriptive composition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.3.1 Essay writing – Descriptive composition, part of Strand 7 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we present information in descriptive writing? 2. Why is it important to consider personal interests when choosing a sport or game?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a text on sports and games from online or print sources,

2. collaborate with peers to identify descriptive words (adjectives) as used in the text,

3. take turns to play a language game

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a text on sports and games from online or print sources,
2. collaborate with peers to identify descriptive words (adjectives) as used in the text,
3. take turns to play a language game

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.3.1 Essay writing – Descriptive composition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: The learner demonstrates tolerance when playing a language game where they describe an object using non- verbal cues and have their peers guess what object it is.

• Digital Literacy: The learner interacts with digital content when reading a text on sports and games from online or print

sources.

Values:
• Integrity: This is nurtured as the learner displays transparency when sharing their composition with peers for review.

• Love: This is promoted as the learner takes turns to play a language game where they describe an object using non-verbal

cues and have their peers guess what object it is.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Civic Responsibility: The learner reviews peers’ work for constructive feedback and helps in presenting the reviewed

compositions in a writing contest.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of specific descriptions of sports and games to their active involvement in Creative Arts

and Sports.
